transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (MetroCore Head of AI), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Ruth Chang (Security), Alex Bae (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Discussed integration patterns for SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex. Customer leaning toward Dedicated for predictable throughput but evaluating Private for regulatory reasons. Need sample integration code, pricing, and SOC2/KMS docs.

Topics: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy, quotas, observability hooks, Private/VPC considerations.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Jenna, I'm the AE on this. With me is Marco, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Marco (Redwood SE): Hi all. I'll try to keep the deep stuff digestible but happy to dive deep — latency, batching, that sort of thing.
[00:18] Lena (MetroCore): Hi, Lena here. We're excited — we've been benchmark-ing a couple providers. Our main ask today is: how do we integrate Redwood into our stack? We're heavy on python, LangChain, and have some repo that uses LlamaIndex, so compatibility is key. Also security and quotas, especially per-tenant limits.
[00:36] Samir (MetroCore): And we need to understand the gateway/proxy patterns — do we front Redwood with our own gateway, or do we route directly? What's recommended for rate limiting and observability?
[00:48] Marco: Great questions. At a high level, there are three deployment patterns: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC or on-prem). For integration, SDKs (python/js) and REST are first-class. We also provide official connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex — though you'll see some docs that call it LamaIndex in spots, sorry for the typo.
[01:10] Jenna: To add, our SDKs handle streaming, function-calling, embeddings, everything you'd expect. Many customers use a thin gateway in front for auth and tenant routing; others talk directly to Redwood using per-tenant API keys.
[01:25] Ruth (MetroCore): For us, the ideal is to keep traffic inside our VPC for PHI-adjacent stuff. If we go Dedicated, can we get a VPC peering option or is that Private-only?
[01:36] Marco: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools but is still hosted; we offer Private for full VPC/on-prem with a customer-managed control plane. For Dedicated we can do network isolation and private endpoints in some regions — we'll confirm the exact peering options for your region.
[01:50] Alex (MetroCore): Architecturally, for LangChain usage, we want to cache embeddings and reuse them with LlamaIndex. Any gotchas? People mention KV cache and prefix caching with Redwood.
[02:02] Marco: Yes — runtime does automatic KV cache for autoregressive sessions; for embeddings you can use our embeddings API and then store them in your vector DB. If you use LangChain or LlamaIndex, the connectors can call Redwood embeddings directly. A common pattern: your gateway handles auth + tenant quotas, proxies to Redwood for inference, and records traces to our observability hooks.
[02:22] Samir: On that gateway question — does Redwood provide a reference proxy implementation? We want to implement rate limiting per tenant and per-route quotas and also enforce request size limits.
[02:33] Marco: We have a sample gateway in our samples repo (link shared after call). It includes token-based routing, JWT examples, and a basic per-tenant rate limiter. For production we recommend using your API gateway (kong/ingress/NGINX/envoy) plus our telemetry endpoint so you can correlate traces and token counts.
[02:49] Lena: What's the token accounting look like? We need token-level cost reporting per request to bill internal teams.
[02:57] Marco: We emit token-level usage in our observability hooks — you can get per-request token counts, latency, model used. In Redwood Console we break down token cost per route and model. For Dedicated/Private we expose the same telemetry to your observability stack via our export hooks (we support Prometheus, Zipkin traces, and a JSON webhook for granular billing).
[03:19] Ruth: From security: KMS integration — can you use our KMS / HSM for model keys and data encryption? Also audit logs and retention?
[03:28] Marco: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. Dedicated has integrations with cloud KMS for key wrapping; we can provide audit logs and forward them into your SIEM. We'll attach SOC 2 docs and the compliance pack.
[03:39] Alex: On SDKs, we use TypeScript on the frontend and python in backend. Are both SDKs mature? Any feature parity issues?
[03:48] Jenna: Both SDKs are feature-parity for most customers. Streaming slight differences historically but we've unified a lot — Marco, anything to call out?
[03:55] Marco: Streaming is supported in both. The python SDK has some advanced helpers for LangChain chains, the JS SDK has similar helpers for function calling. We'll share code samples. Note: if you use a third-party chain library, watch for websocket semantics and the way streaming chunks are emitted — small differences in chunking may require a tiny adapter.
[04:16] Samir: Rate limits — we need to support burst behavior for some real-time flows. If we have per-tenant burst up to X qps and sustained Y qps, can Redwood handle that without drastically increasing cost?
[04:28] Marco: Yes, quotas are configurable per-tenant. For Dedicated you can reserve capacity for baseline throughput and allow bursts to Hosted pool, or configure burst capacity options. Costs depend on reserved vs burst usage; our Optimize tooling can recommend batching/quantization to reduce tokens and cost.
[04:45] Lena: We're using LangChain Memory and LlamaIndex nodes to build context windows. Does Redwood have any guidance on managing KV cache vs LlamaIndex local caches? People worry about stale context and cache invalidation.
[04:59] Marco: Good point. KV cache in our runtime is ephemeral for active sessions; for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) flows with LlamaIndex, your vector DB is the source of truth. Many teams do a hybrid: keep active session KV in runtime for latency, and persist long-term context in LlamaIndex/DB. We'll share a best-practices doc.
[05:16] Jenna: Quick clarifying Q: are you planning to run the POC on Hosted or Dedicated?
[05:20] Lena: We're leaning Dedicated for predictable latency, but Security might push Private later if compliance requires it. So POC on Dedicated would be ideal.
[05:28] Ruth: we'll need to see encryption in transit and at rest and an attestation that logs can be forwarded. Also SSO/SAML integration for RBAC.
[05:38] Marco: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in the Console. Audit logs can be streamed. For Dedicated we provide tenant-level RBAC and token scopes.
[05:47] Samir: About observability hooks — do we get traces per token or per request only? We want to attribute cost to feature owners.
[05:55] Marco: You get both. Per-request traces include token deltas and model profile. We can push a webhook that contains itemized token counts and an estimated cost per call. That integrates nicely into your internal billing pipeline.
[06:08] Alex: Any limits on webhook throughput? We might produce thousands of events per minute in peak.
[06:15] Marco: Our telemetry export is rate-limited; for very high-volume customers we recommend batching to an internal collector (e.g., Kafka) and then forwarding to Redwood's ingest. For Dedicated/Private we can tune that ingest path. We'll follow up with recommended ingestion architecture.
[06:30] Lena: Let's talk LangChain specifics — we've got existing chains that call OpenAI, Anthropic, and local models. If we switch to Redwood for some routes, will the LangChain wrappers work as drop-in?
[06:42] Marco: We provide LangChain wrappers that mimic the OpenAI API so many chains are drop-in. For Anthropic/other differences, there can be subtle prompt-shaping differences; part of POC is to run a diff on outputs. Also note that model variants and quantized builds can affect output distribution.
[07:01] Samir: On the topic of model rollout — can we pin model versions per route so a single API route uses a specific model?
[07:09] Marco: Yes, per-route model pinning is supported in the Console. You can do canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallbacks to compatible variants when capacity is constrained.
[07:20] Lena: Our latency SLOs are tight for chat flows — sub 200ms 95th for short prompts. Do you have benchmarks for that on Dedicated?
[07:30] Marco: We have verified latency profiles in our model catalog; dedicated pools tuned for small sequence lengths generally meet sub-200ms for shorter prompts on certain GPUs. We'll share the model performance sheet; note results vary by sequence length and batch behavior.
[07:46] Jenna: I'm going to share the pricing sheet and the SLA after this call. Marco will attach integration samples.
[07:52] Ruth: A question about data retention and deletion for Private vs Dedicated — if a tenant requests deletion, how quickly is data purged from caches and logs?
[08:02] Marco: For Private you can control retention directly. For Dedicated we support configurable retention windows; ephemeral KV caches are short-lived, and logs can be purged per retention policy — we'll include standard retention options in the compliance pack.
[08:13] Samir: Anything we should watch for when using LlamaIndex connectors? There was a bug noted in older connectors.
[08:20] Marco: We recently updated the connectors; older versions had a deserialization mismatch with certain index schemas. Use the latest connector; we'll include the pinned version in the sample repo.
[08:31] Lena: On quotas again, what's the enforcement behavior? Do you return 429s or queue requests? We prefer graceful degradation rather than hard rejects for some flows.
[08:41] Marco: Options are configurable. You can apply soft quotas that throttle and queue for short bursts, or hard limits that return 429. For critical paths we recommend setting a high soft quota and then a fallback model or cached answer. Redwood's routing can automatically fallback to smaller model variants when capacity is low.
[08:58] Alex: For our billing, we need CSV exports of per-route token usage daily. Is that available?
[09:05] Marco: Yes, daily exports are available. You can also hit the usage API to pull per-route/per-tenant metrics programmatically.
[09:12] Jenna: Quick note: we'll share links to the LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and a reference gateway. Also we'll include the SOC2 summary and KMS integration docs.
[09:21] Lena: That sounds good. On timeline: we want a short POC — 3 weeks to validate latency, cost, and LangChain compatibility. Does that align?
[09:30] Jenna: Yes, that's reasonable. Our POC playbook typically runs 2-4 weeks. We'll propose a 3-week plan in the follow-up.
[09:37] Samir: One more infra Q — is there a recommended way to do request-level feature flags? We want to route only a subset of traffic to Redwood initially.
[09:46] Marco: Use your gateway to do traffic splitting; our pricing and metrics will reflect which routes go to Redwood. In the Console you can tag routes for cost attribution. We also support canary routing in Dedicated so you can route a percentage to a new model.
[09:59] Ruth: Security sign-off will need an architecture diagram and the SOC2 pack. We'll email those questions to Jenna.
[10:06] Jenna: Perfect. For next steps I'll send pricing/SLA and Marco will send code samples. We'll schedule a POC kickoff once you review.
[10:14] Lena: Thanks all. A couple of small transcription artifacts I've seen in other calls — you might see Redwood product names transcribed oddly, like Redwood Dedicate or K-V cash, but that's fine.
[10:24] Marco: (laughs) Yeah our product names love to be misspelled.
[10:28] Alex: Ok that's it from us. Thanks.
[10:31] Jenna: Quick recap — action items: Jenna send pricing + SLA, Marco send LangChain/LlamaIndex & gateway samples, Samir to provide traffic profile, Ruth to send security question list. We'll aim to reconvene after you've reviewed materials and confirm POC scope.
[10:47] Lena: Great, thanks everyone.
[10:50] End of call.

Notes: occasionally the auto-transcription mis-labels LlamaIndex as LamaIndex, KV cache as K-V cash, and Redwood Dedicated as Redwood Dedicate. Customer wants POC on Dedicated and potential move to Private pending security review.
